newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity prices up on physicals, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity prices up on physicals, weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Wednesday with the majority of activity in the Palo Verde contract due to strong Southwest physical prices and expectations of continued warm weather, sources said.
Strength in power futures was also coming from some skepticism over expected restart dates for the two San Onofre nuclear power units in California, the sources said.
"Everybody who bet on these units (in the U.S. West) coming back on time is hurting now," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1220 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 55 cents at $36.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trades in a range of $35.85-36.25, while September was trading up 57 cents at $30.10 following exchanges at $29.80-30.25 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 26 cents at $23.50 after trades at $23.30-$23.70, while September was up 45 cents at the day's high of $23.40 following trade as low as $23.10 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1135 EDT an estimated total of 151 PV and 66 COB contracts had traded.
Western physical power prices were said to be strong based on transmission problems on the Pacific Intertie and some forecasts of warm weather in the Southwest, sources said.
Next-day PV peak power was trading at over $40 per MWh, while balance of July peak power was talked near $36.25, sources said.
"With the higher short term numbers we're seeing some utility interest on the buy side for August," the Houston-based source said.
In generation news, restarts of the 1,070 megawatt (MW) unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating (SONG) Station, in San Clemente, Calif., were set for July 15 and July 17.

SONG 2 was shut June 29 to replace charge line check valves, while SONG 3 has been out of service since April 12 for refueling, maintenance and replacement work. An original restart date for SONG 3 was pushed back from near July 10.

Also, the 1,073 MW unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant was expected to remain at 75 percent power Wednesday pending results of further analysis and monitoring, plant operator Pacific Gas & Electric Co said.

The unit, located at Avila Beach on California's central coast, had been expected to reach full power late Tuesday after being manually shut a week ago due to a problem with its feedwater system. No information was immediately available on how long the unit would remain curtailed.
Power production at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was still around 15 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday, with the unit expected to be on line later this week.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 2 in Nevada, which tripped off line Monday due to a tube leak, was scheduled to restart later today.
Meteorologists called for cool, wet weather to linger over the Pacific Northwest into the weekend, followed by warmer, drier conditions next week.

Forecasters were split in their outlook for the Southwest. Some expected arid, seasonal weather to stay in the region through next week, while others predicted very hot weather stretching from California to much of Midwest.
As of 1225 EDT, NYMEX August Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 2.4 cents at $2.092 per million British thermal units.
